suites.rootCause: TEST-METHODOLOGY MISMATCH, not a port bug — this suite mocks the network by stubbing a `curl` binary on PATH; the port's bin/llm.mjs calls Node's native `fetch()` directly (src/llm.ts:92) and never shells out to curl (PARITY.md Deviations: "llm transport-failure wording ... there is no curl"). The stub is never invoked, so every request that should have been intercepted instead makes a REAL connection attempt to 127.0.0.1:9, which Node's fetch (undici) refuses outright — port 9 is on the fetch-spec's forbidden-port list (`ERR_UNDICI ... bad port`), where curl has no such restriction. No assertion here exercises port-owned logic; the whole suite needs a fetch-level interceptor (e.g. undici MockAgent) to be a valid oracle for the port, which is out of scope for this runner (no src/*.ts or harness edits).

The port's actual OpenRouter-routing behavior IS independently proven: parity/llm/run-parity.mjs's `or-routing` scenario group (25 cases, mirroring every assertion in this suite 1:1) runs both the real Bash and the port against a real local HTTP server and diffs the request JSON byte-for-byte — 25/25 PARITY, 0 port bugs (see PARITY.md's Upstream sync 1b section).

(a) 2 assertions ('status.sh PATTERNS == headlong-killall PATTERNS', both 'dash pattern: killall == status.sh/uninstall.sh') `sed`-extract tools/headlong-killall's OWN BASH SOURCE TEXT (its `PATTERNS=(...)`/`DASH_PAT=` array literals) and compare it against status.sh/uninstall.sh's embedded copies — a pure source-text-equality check with no subprocess involved. Substituting tools/headlong-killall with a one-line Node-dispatching wrapper (`exec node .../headlong-killall.mjs "$@"`, no PATTERNS array to extract) makes these fail by construction — same class as the existing test_mem_frontmatter.sh bash-artifact-dependency row. (b) the 'clone' failure: the 'install:' block runs `git clone -q --local "$REPO" "$APP"`, but this runner's lightweight scratch copy (tests/bin/thinkers/tools[/deploy] only, following the SAME technique every other suite in this file uses) never copies a `.git` directory at all, so the scratch root is not a git repository and the clone fails outright — the script's own `|| { bad "clone"; exit 1; }` then aborts the ENTIRE suite immediately, which is why port shows 'exit=1 (no pass/fail line)' instead of a real N/M count; every downstream assertion (18 of them) never runs as a result. This is a limitation of this runner's scratch-copy technique for the one suite that happens to `git clone` its own REPO variable, not a port behavior bug — a full git-backed scratch checkout would cost copying the ~360MB upstream tree (web/, tui/) per run and was judged not worth it for this lane.

daemon.rootCause: BASH-ARTIFACT DEPENDENCY, not a port bug — the four failures are the two cases that inject the crash through a shim on the dispatcher's PATH (an `mv` shim that does `kill -9 $PPID` the moment the claim lands in run/claimed/, and an `rm` shim that does it when the sent receipt is about to be removed). The port's dispatcher renames and unlinks with fs calls inside one Node process: no `mv`/`rm` child ever runs, so the shim never fires ('no crash flag, shim log: ' is empty) and the downstream record/receipt checks have nothing to observe. The same two windows (die after the claim, die after the send with the receipt still on disk) are exercised on the port side by THINKERS_TEST_DIE_AFTER_CLAIM and the dieHook in test/dispatcherReceipts.test.ts. The flock lifetime-lock cases are skipped upstream-style on this host (no flock(1) on macOS), and the port has no flock analogue by design — ownership is the 16-byte token plus a pid-alive guard (PARITY.md, lane f).
